questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: An aqueous solution containing $0.10\text{ mol}$ of hypophosphorous acid ($\text{H}_3\text{PO}_2$) and $0.10\text{ mol}$ of orthophosphorous acid ($\text{H}_3\text{PO}_3$) is divided into two equal aliquots. Aliquot 1 is titrated to complete neutralization with standard aqueous $\text{NaOH}$. Aliquot 2 is treated with excess aqueous silver nitrate ($\text{AgNO}_3$). What are the moles of $\text{NaOH}$ consumed in Aliquot 1 and the moles of metallic $\text{Ag}$ precipitated in Aliquot 2, respectively?
options: A) $0.30\text{ mol }\text{NaOH}$ and $0.60\text{ mol }\text{Ag}$
B) $0.20\text{ mol }\text{NaOH}$ and $0.40\text{ mol }\text{Ag}$
C) $0.15\text{ mol }\text{NaOH}$ and $0.30\text{ mol }\text{Ag}$
D) $0.30\text{ mol }\text{NaOH}$ and $0.30\text{ mol }\text{Ag}$
questions.explanation: Step 1 involves basicity determination. $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_2$ possesses one ionizable $\text{P-OH}$ bond (monobasic), whereas $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_3$ possesses two $\text{P-OH}$ bonds (dibasic). In the initial solution, total ionizable protons equal $0.10(1) + 0.10(2) = 0.30\text{ mol}$. Since Aliquot 1 is exactly half of the initial solution, substituting this fraction yields $\frac{0.30}{2} = 0.15\text{ mol}$ of $\text{NaOH}$ required. Step 2 requires determining reducing capacity. Each $\text{P-H}$ bond acts as a reducing center. $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_2$ has two $\text{P-H}$ bonds ($P^{+1} \to P^{+5}$, losing $4e^-$ per molecule, thus reducing $4\text{ Ag}^+$), and $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_3$ has one $\text{P-H}$ bond ($P^{+3} \to P^{+5}$, losing $2e^-$, reducing $2\text{ Ag}^+$). In the initial solution, total $\text{Ag}$ precipitated is $0.10(4) + 0.10(2) = 0.60\text{ mol}$. Therefore, in Aliquot 2, dividing by two yields $0.30\text{ mol}$ of $\text{Ag}$. Hence, $0.15\text{ mol }\text{NaOH}$ and $0.30\text{ mol }\text{Ag}$ are obtained. Forgetting to divide by two for the aliquot produces $0.30\text{ mol}$ and $0.60\text{ mol}$, while assuming both acids are tribasic gives $0.30\text{ mol }\text{NaOH}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Phosphorus pentachloride in the solid state exists as an ionic compound $[\text{PCl}_4]^+[\text{PCl}_6]^-$, whereas solid phosphorus pentabromide exists as $[\text{PBr}_4]^+[\text{Br}]^-$. If a crystalline equimolar mixture containing $1.0\text{ mol}$ of solid $\text{PCl}_5$ and $1.0\text{ mol}$ of solid $\text{PBr}_5$ is analyzed, what are the total moles of phosphorus atoms exhibiting $sp^3d^2$ hybridization and the total moles of uncoordinated, monoatomic halide anions present in the lattice, respectively?
options: A) $0.5\text{ mol}$ of $sp^3d^2$ hybridized $\text{P}$ atoms and $1.0\text{ mol}$ of uncoordinated halide anions
B) $1.0\text{ mol}$ of $sp^3d^2$ hybridized $\text{P}$ atoms and $0.5\text{ mol}$ of uncoordinated halide anions
C) $0.5\text{ mol}$ of $sp^3d^2$ hybridized $\text{P}$ atoms and $0.5\text{ mol}$ of uncoordinated halide anions
D) $1.0\text{ mol}$ of $sp^3d^2$ hybridized $\text{P}$ atoms and $1.0\text{ mol}$ of uncoordinated halide anions
questions.explanation: Step 1 examines the ionic dissociation of solid phosphorus pentachloride. One mole of solid $\text{PCl}_5$ dissociates into $0.5\text{ mol}$ of tetrahedral $[\text{PCl}_4]^+$ cations ($sp^3$ hybridized) and $0.5\text{ mol}$ of octahedral $[\text{PCl}_6]^-$ anions ($sp^3d^2$ hybridized with steric number 6). Therefore, the number of $sp^3d^2$ hybridized phosphorus atoms is exactly $0.5\text{ mol}$. Step 2 examines solid phosphorus pentabromide. Due to severe steric crowding of the large bromine atoms, phosphorus cannot accommodate six bromines to form $[\text{PBr}_6]^-$. Hence, solid $\text{PBr}_5$ crystallizes as $1.0\text{ mol}$ of tetrahedral $[\text{PBr}_4]^+$ cations ($sp^3$) and $1.0\text{ mol}$ of monoatomic bromide anions $[\text{Br}]^-$. Applying this constraint, the total number of uncoordinated halide anions is $1.0\text{ mol}$ of $\text{Br}^-$, as all chlorine atoms remain covalently bound within the coordination shells. Solving together yields $0.5\text{ mol}$ and $1.0\text{ mol}$. Assuming solid $\text{PCl}_5$ yields $1.0\text{ mol}$ of anion overlooks the stoichiometry of the $[\text{PCl}_4]^+[\text{PCl}_6]^-$ ion pair.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Complete hydrolysis of $1.0\text{ mol}$ of iodine pentafluoride ($\text{IF}_5$) and $1.0\text{ mol}$ of bromine trifluoride ($\text{BrF}_3$) in water produces hydrofluoric acid alongside the respective oxoacids of iodine and bromine. What is the total mass of $\text{HF}$ formed (molar mass $= 20.0\text{ g/mol}$) and the sum of the oxidation states of iodine and bromine in their isolated oxoacid hydrolysis products?
options: A) $140.0\text{ g}$ of $\text{HF}$ and sum of oxidation states $+7$
B) $160.0\text{ g}$ of $\text{HF}$ and sum of oxidation states $+8$
C) $160.0\text{ g}$ of $\text{HF}$ and sum of oxidation states $+10$
D) $120.0\text{ g}$ of $\text{HF}$ and sum of oxidation states $+8$
questions.explanation: Step 1 considers the hydrolysis reaction of $\text{IF}_5$: $\text{IF}_5 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O} \to \text{HIO}_3 + 5\text{HF}$. Hydrolysis of an interhalogen compound $\text{XX'}_n$ produces the hydrohalic acid of the smaller, more electronegative halogen $\text{X'}$ and the oxoacid of the larger halogen $\text{X}$ in which the central halogen retains its oxidation state. Here, iodine remains in the $+5$ oxidation state in iodic acid ($\text{HIO}_3$), yielding $5.0\text{ mol}$ of $\text{HF}$. Step 2 considers the hydrolysis of $\text{BrF}_3$: $\text{BrF}_3 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \to \text{HBrO}_2 + 3\text{HF}$. In bromous acid ($\text{HBrO}_2$), bromine retains its $+3$ oxidation state, yielding $3.0\text{ mol}$ of $\text{HF}$. Therefore, total moles of $\text{HF} = 5.0 + 3.0 = 8.0\text{ mol}$. Substituting the molar mass gives mass $= 8.0\text{ mol} \times 20.0\text{ g/mol} = 160.0\text{ g}$. Hence, the sum of oxidation states of the central halogens is $+5 + (+3) = +8$. An answer of $140.0\text{ g}$ results from misbalancing the fluorine stoichiometry, while $+10$ erroneously assumes oxidation of both halogens to $+5$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: A gas stream containing ozone ($\text{O}_3$) is passed through an excess of neutral potassium iodide solution buffered with borate buffer at $\text{pH} = 9.2$. The liberated iodine is titrated with $0.050\text{ M}$ standard sodium thiosulfate solution, requiring exactly $40.0\text{ mL}$ for complete decolorization using starch indicator. What is the volume of pure ozone gas present in the initial sample measured at STP (molar volume $= 22400\text{ mL/mol}$)?
options: A) $44.8\text{ mL}$
B) $11.2\text{ mL}$
C) $89.6\text{ mL}$
D) $22.4\text{ mL}$
questions.explanation: Step 1 establishes the redox stoichiometry between ozone and iodide: $\text{O}_3 + 2\text{I}^- + \text{H}_2\text{O} \to \text{O}_2 + \text{I}_2 + 2\text{OH}^-$. This reaction indicates that $1\text{ mol}$ of $\text{O}_3$ quantitatively liberates $1\text{ mol}$ of $\text{I}_2$. Step 2 evaluates the iodometric titration: $\text{I}_2 + 2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-} \to 2\text{I}^- + \text{S}_4\text{O}_6^{2-}$, which shows that $1\text{ mol}$ of $\text{I}_2$ reacts with $2\text{ mol}$ of $\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-}$. Solving for moles of thiosulfate gives $n(\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-}) = 0.0400\text{ L} \times 0.050\text{ mol/L} = 2.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ mol}$. Therefore, moles of iodine liberated equal $\frac{2.0 \times 10^{-3}}{2} = 1.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ mol}$. Substituting this value yields $n(\text{O}_3) = 1.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ mol}$. Hence, volume at STP $= 1.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ mol} \times 22400\text{ mL/mol} = 22.4\text{ mL}$. An answer of $44.8\text{ mL}$ forgets the stoichiometric factor of $2$ for thiosulfate, while $11.2\text{ mL}$ applies the factor of $2$ twice.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In tetraphosphorus decaoxide ($\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$), let $x$ be the number of bridging $\text{P-O-P}$ bonds and $y$ be the number of terminal $\text{P=O}$ double bonds. In one molecule of cyclotrimetaphosphoric acid ($(\text{HPO}_3)_3$), let $z$ be the number of bridging $\text{P-O-P}$ bonds. Calculate the integer value of $(2x + y - z)$.
questions.explanation: Step 1 analyzes the cage structure of $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$. The four phosphorus atoms define the vertices of a tetrahedron. Each of the six edges contains a bridging oxygen atom, giving $x = 6$ bridging $\text{P-O-P}$ bonds. Each phosphorus also forms one coordinate/double bond to an external terminal oxygen, yielding $y = 4$ terminal $\text{P=O}$ bonds. Step 2 examines the cyclic structure of cyclotrimetaphosphoric acid ($(\text{HPO}_3)_3$). The trimer forms a six-membered alternating ring consisting of three phosphorus atoms and three oxygen atoms ($-\text{P}-\text{O}-\text{P}-\text{O}-\text{P}-\text{O}-$). Therefore, the ring contains $z = 3$ bridging $\text{P-O-P}$ bonds. Substituting these parameters into the formula gives $(2x + y - z) = 2(6) + 4 - 3 = 12 + 4 - 3 = 13$. Hence, the calculated integer value is 13.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: When white phosphorus ($\text{P}_4$) is boiled with concentrated aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ solution under an inert atmosphere of $\text{CO}_2$, it undergoes disproportionation according to: $\text{P}_4 + 3\text{NaOH} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O} \to \text{PH}_3 + 3\text{NaH}_2\text{PO}_2$. What fraction of the total phosphorus atoms undergoes oxidation, and what is the equivalent weight of $\text{P}_4$ in this redox reaction in terms of its molar mass $M$?
options: A) $\frac{3}{4}$ of phosphorus atoms oxidized and equivalent weight $\frac{M}{3}$
B) $\frac{1}{4}$ of phosphorus atoms oxidized and equivalent weight $\frac{M}{3}$
C) $\frac{3}{4}$ of phosphorus atoms oxidized and equivalent weight $\frac{M}{4}$
D) $\frac{1}{2}$ of phosphorus atoms oxidized and equivalent weight $\frac{M}{2}$
questions.explanation: Step 1 identifies the changes in oxidation state of phosphorus. In elemental $\text{P}_4$, the oxidation number of phosphorus is $0$. In phosphine ($\text{PH}_3$), the oxidation number is $-3$ (reduction: $0 \to -3$, gain of 3 electrons). In sodium hypophosphite ($\text{NaH}_2\text{PO}_2$), the oxidation number is $+1$ (oxidation: $0 \to +1$, loss of 1 electron). Step 2 tracks atomic stoichiometry: out of the 4 phosphorus atoms in $\text{P}_4$, 3 atoms are oxidized to $\text{H}_2\text{PO}_2^-$ while 1 atom is reduced to $\text{PH}_3$. Therefore, the fraction of phosphorus atoms oxidized is $\frac{3}{4}$. Step 3 evaluates the total electron transfer: 3 phosphorus atoms each lose 1 electron, yielding a total of $3$ moles of electrons transferred per mole of $\text{P}_4$ consumed. Hence, the n-factor of $\text{P}_4$ is $n = 3$, meaning the equivalent weight is $\frac{M}{3}$. Solving together leads to $\frac{3}{4}$ and $\frac{M}{3}$. The distractor $\frac{1}{4}$ refers to the reduced fraction, while an equivalent weight of $\frac{M}{4}$ incorrectly uses the total atom count as the n-factor.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the series of Group 16 hydrides: $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, $\text{H}_2\text{S}$, $\text{H}_2\text{Se}$, and $\text{H}_2\text{Te}$. As one progresses down the group from $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ to $\text{H}_2\text{Te}$, which statement accurately justifies the observed simultaneous increase in both acidic strength and reducing capacity?
options: A) Both properties increase because the $\text{H-E}$ bond dissociation enthalpy decreases markedly from oxygen to tellurium
B) Acidic strength increases due to increasing electronegativity of the central atom, whereas reducing capacity increases due to lower bond polarity
C) Acidic strength increases because the conjugate base becomes less stable, while reducing capacity increases due to higher bond enthalpy
D) Reducing capacity increases because of intermolecular hydrogen bonding, while acidic strength increases due to smaller ionic radius
questions.explanation: Step 1 examines the variation in bond parameters down Group 16. As the atomic size of the central chalcogen increases ($\text{O} < \text{S} < \text{Se} < \text{Te}$), the orbital overlap with the small $1s$ orbital of hydrogen becomes increasingly diffuse and inefficient. Consequently, the $\text{H-E}$ bond dissociation enthalpy decreases sharply from $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ ($463\text{ kJ/mol}$) to $\text{H}_2\text{Te}$ ($269\text{ kJ/mol}$). Step 2 links bond strength to acidity. A lower $\text{H-E}$ bond dissociation enthalpy allows proton release in aqueous solution to occur much more readily, yielding an increase in acid dissociation constant: $K_a(\text{H}_2\text{O}) < K_a(\text{H}_2\text{S}) < K_a(\text{H}_2\text{Se}) < K_a(\text{H}_2\text{Te})$. Step 3 links bond strength to reducing action. Decreased thermal stability and weaker $\text{H-E}$ bonds imply that tellurium hydride readily dissociates to furnish hydrogen, making $\text{H}_2\text{Te}$ the strongest reducing agent in the series. Therefore, both trends are driven by decreasing bond dissociation enthalpy. Hence, statement A is correct. Electronegativity decreases down the group, so attributing higher acidity to electronegativity is conceptually erroneous.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Complete hydrolysis of solid xenon difluoride proceeds according to: $2\text{XeF}_2(s) + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(l) \to 2\text{Xe}(g) + \text{O}_2(g) + 4\text{HF}(aq)$. If $0.40\text{ mol}$ of $\text{XeF}_2$ undergoes complete reaction, what is the total volume of dry gaseous products collected at STP (molar volume $= 22.4\text{ L/mol}$) and the change in oxidation number of the element that undergoes oxidation?
options: A) $8.96\text{ L}$ of gas and oxidation number increases by $4$
B) $17.92\text{ L}$ of gas and oxidation number increases by $1$
C) $13.44\text{ L}$ of gas and oxidation number increases by $2$
D) $4.48\text{ L}$ of gas and oxidation number increases by $2$
questions.explanation: Step 1 evaluates the molar amounts of gaseous products formed from $0.40\text{ mol}$ of $\text{XeF}_2$. Based on the stoichiometric coefficients, $2\text{ mol}$ of $\text{XeF}_2$ produce $2\text{ mol}$ of $\text{Xe}(g)$ and $1\text{ mol}$ of $\text{O}_2(g)$, while $\text{HF}$ remains dissolved in the aqueous phase. Solving for the gaseous products yields $n(\text{Xe}) = 0.40\text{ mol}$ and $n(\text{O}_2) = \frac{0.40}{2} = 0.20\text{ mol}$. Therefore, the total moles of dry gas collected equal $0.40 + 0.20 = 0.60\text{ mol}$. Step 2 converts moles to STP volume: substituting the molar volume gives $V = 0.60\text{ mol} \times 22.4\text{ L/mol} = 13.44\text{ L}$. Step 3 tracks the oxidation number changes. Xenon is reduced from $+2$ in $\text{XeF}_2$ to $0$ in elemental $\text{Xe}$. Oxygen in water is oxidized from $-2$ to $0$ in $\text{O}_2$. Hence, the oxidation number of oxygen increases by $2$ units (from $-2$ to $0$). An answer of $8.96\text{ L}$ neglects oxygen gas, while $17.92\text{ L}$ mistakenly counts $\text{HF}$ as an ideal dry gas.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider one molecule of peroxomonosulfuric acid (Caro's acid, $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_5$) and one molecule of peroxodisulfuric acid (Marshall's acid, $\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_8$). Let $N_{\text{peroxy}}$ be the total count of peroxo oxygen atoms (oxidation state $-1$) combined across both molecules, and let $N_{\text{S(VI)}}$ be the total count of sulfur atoms possessing a $+6$ oxidation state across both molecules. Calculate the integer product $(N_{\text{peroxy}} \times N_{\text{S(VI)}})$.
questions.explanation: Step 1 analyzes Caro's acid ($\text{H}_2\text{SO}_5$). Its Lewis structure is $\text{HO}-\text{SO}_2-\text{O}-\text{O}-\text{H}$. It contains one peroxo linkage ($-O-O-$), which contributes $2$ peroxo oxygen atoms with oxidation number $-1$. The remaining three oxygens are oxo/hydroxy oxygens with oxidation number $-2$. Applying charge neutrality: $2(+1) + S + 2(-1) + 3(-2) = 0 \implies S = +6$. Thus, Caro's acid contains $1$ sulfur atom in the $+6$ state. Step 2 analyzes Marshall's acid ($\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_8$). Its structure is $\text{HO}-\text{SO}_2-\text{O}-\text{O}-\text{SO}_2-\text{OH}$, featuring one central bridging peroxo linkage containing $2$ peroxo oxygen atoms ($-1$ each). Both sulfur atoms reside in identical tetrahedral coordination environments with oxidation state $+6$, giving $2$ sulfur atoms in the $+6$ state. Step 3 sums the quantities: $N_{\text{peroxy}} = 2 + 2 = 4$, and $N_{\text{S(VI)}} = 1 + 2 = 3$. Therefore, substituting these counts into the product yields $4 \times 3 = 12$. Hence, the result is 12.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Xenon tetrafluoride ($\text{XeF}_4$) is synthesized by heating xenon and fluorine in a $1:5$ molar ratio at $873\text{ K}$ and $7\text{ bar}$. When solid $\text{XeF}_4$ is treated with excess liquid water at room temperature, it undergoes disproportionation: $6\text{XeF}_4 + 12\text{H}_2\text{O} \to 4\text{Xe} + 2\text{XeO}_3 + 24\text{HF} + 3\text{O}_2$. If $1.20\text{ mol}$ of $\text{XeF}_4$ is hydrolyzed completely, what are the moles of solid $\text{XeO}_3$ produced and the total moles of electrons transferred in this redox disproportionation, respectively?
options: A) $0.20\text{ mol }\text{XeO}_3$ and $1.60\text{ mol }e^-$
B) $0.40\text{ mol }\text{XeO}_3$ and $3.20\text{ mol }e^-$
C) $0.40\text{ mol }\text{XeO}_3$ and $2.40\text{ mol }e^-$
D) $0.80\text{ mol }\text{XeO}_3$ and $3.20\text{ mol }e^-$
questions.explanation: Step 1 calculates the stoichiometric yield of $\text{XeO}_3$. From the balanced equation, $6\text{ mol}$ of $\text{XeF}_4$ produce $2\text{ mol}$ of $\text{XeO}_3$. Therefore, for $1.20\text{ mol}$ of $\text{XeF}_4$, substituting into the ratio yields $n(\text{XeO}_3) = \frac{2}{6} \times 1.20 = 0.40\text{ mol}$. Step 2 evaluates the redox electron transfer. In $\text{XeF}_4$, the oxidation state of $\text{Xe}$ is $+4$. It disproportionates into elemental $\text{Xe}^0$ and $\text{XeO}_3$ (where $\text{Xe}$ is $+6$). Reduction of xenon: $4\text{ mol}$ of $\text{Xe}$ are reduced from $+4$ to $0$ per $6\text{ mol}$ of $\text{XeF}_4$, requiring $4 \times 4 = 16\text{ mol}$ of electrons per $6\text{ mol}$ of $\text{XeF}_4$. For $1.20\text{ mol}$ of $\text{XeF}_4$, the moles of electrons transferred equal $\frac{16}{6} \times 1.20 = 3.20\text{ mol}$. Applying oxidation tracking confirms this: $0.40\text{ mol}$ of $\text{Xe}$ loses $2e^-$ ($0.80\text{ mol }e^-$) and $0.60\text{ mol}$ of $\text{O}_2$ is formed by loss of $4e^-$ per $\text{O}_2$ ($2.40\text{ mol }e^-$), giving $0.80 + 2.40 = 3.20\text{ mol }e^-$. Hence, $0.40\text{ mol}$ and $3.20\text{ mol}$ are obtained. An answer of $0.20\text{ mol}$ arises from incorrectly halving the stoichiometric fraction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The experimental bond dissociation enthalpies of diatomic halogen molecules follow the order $\text{Cl}_2 (242.6\text{ kJ/mol}) > \text{Br}_2 (192.8\text{ kJ/mol}) > \text{F}_2 (158.8\text{ kJ/mol}) > \text{I}_2 (151.1\text{ kJ/mol})$. Despite this anomaly, fluorine is by far the strongest oxidizing agent in aqueous solution ($E^\circ = +2.87\text{ V}$). Which statement correctly identifies the combination of thermodynamic factors responsible for this behavior?
options: A) Exceptionally high electron gain enthalpy of fluorine and low hydration enthalpy of fluoride ion
B) High polarizability of the fluorine molecule coupled with weak hydration of the large fluoride ion
C) High ionization energy of fluorine combined with low bond dissociation enthalpy of chlorine
D) Low bond dissociation enthalpy of $\text{F}_2$ due to lone-pair repulsions and an exceptionally large negative hydration enthalpy of $\text{F}^-$
questions.explanation: Step 1 examines the anomalous bond enthalpy of $\text{F}_2$. Because fluorine atoms are small, the three non-bonding lone pairs on each fluorine atom in $\text{F}_2$ are crowded closely together, resulting in significant interelectronic repulsions that weaken the $\text{F-F}$ single covalent bond ($158.8\text{ kJ/mol}$ vs $242.6\text{ kJ/mol}$ for $\text{Cl}_2$). Step 2 evaluates the standard reduction potential cycle: $\frac{1}{2}\text{X}_2(g) + e^- \to \text{X}^-(aq)$, where $\Delta H = \frac{1}{2}\Delta_{\text{diss}}H^\circ + \Delta_{\text{eg}}H^\circ + \Delta_{\text{hyd}}H^\circ$. Although the electron gain enthalpy of chlorine is more negative than that of fluorine ($-349\text{ kJ/mol}$ vs $-333\text{ kJ/mol}$), the smaller radius of $\text{F}^-$ results in an enormous negative hydration enthalpy ($\Delta_{\text{hyd}}H^\circ = -515\text{ kJ/mol}$ for $\text{F}^-$ vs $-381\text{ kJ/mol}$ for $\text{Cl}^-$). Therefore, the combination of low dissociation enthalpy and extremely large negative hydration enthalpy provides the massive driving force. Hence, statement D is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Gaseous brown nitrogen dioxide ($\text{NO}_2$) dimerizes into colorless dinitrogen tetroxide ($\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$) according to the equilibrium: $2\text{NO}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons \text{N}_2\text{O}_4(g) \quad (\Delta H^\circ = -57.2\text{ kJ/mol})$. If an equilibrium mixture maintained in a sealed rigid vessel is cooled from $350\text{ K}$ to $273\text{ K}$, what changes are observed in the total system pressure and the magnetic nature of the mixture?
options: A) Total pressure increases and magnetic susceptibility increases
B) Total pressure decreases and magnetic susceptibility decreases
C) Total pressure decreases and magnetic susceptibility increases
D) Total pressure remains constant while the mixture becomes purely ferromagnetic
questions.explanation: Step 1 applies Le Chatelier's principle to temperature variation. The dimerization reaction is exothermic ($\Delta H^\circ = -57.2\text{ kJ/mol}$). Lowering the temperature from $350\text{ K}$ to $273\text{ K}$ shifts the equilibrium toward the forward direction, favoring the formation of $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$. Step 2 evaluates pressure changes. Two moles of gas combine to form one mole of gas, decreasing the total number of gaseous moles ($n$). Applying the ideal gas equation $P = \frac{nRT}{V}$, both the decrease in temperature $T$ and the decrease in moles $n$ work in tandem to cause a significant decrease in total pressure. Step 3 examines the magnetic properties. $\text{NO}_2$ contains an odd number of valence electrons (23 electrons), resulting in an unpaired electron on nitrogen that renders it paramagnetic. In $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$, the unpaired electrons pair up to form an $\text{N-N}$ single bond, making it diamagnetic. As $\text{NO}_2$ is converted to $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$, the concentration of unpaired electrons drops, meaning magnetic susceptibility decreases. Therefore, both pressure and magnetic susceptibility decrease. Hence, option B is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Determine the total count of non-bonding lone pairs residing exclusively on the central atoms across the following five chemical species: $\text{XeF}_2$, $\text{XeF}_4$, $\text{XeF}_6$, $\text{ClF}_3$, and $\text{BrF}_5$. Calculate the sum of these central lone pairs.
questions.explanation: Step 1 applies VSEPR theory to xenon compounds. Xenon possesses 8 valence electrons. In $\text{XeF}_2$, xenon forms 2 single bonds with fluorine, leaving $8 - 2 = 6$ non-bonding electrons, which corresponds to $3$ lone pairs (linear geometry, $sp^3d$). In $\text{XeF}_4$, xenon forms 4 single bonds, leaving $8 - 4 = 4$ non-bonding electrons, yielding $2$ lone pairs (square planar geometry, $sp^3d^2$). In $\text{XeF}_6$, xenon forms 6 single bonds, leaving $8 - 6 = 2$ electrons, which equals $1$ lone pair (distorted octahedral, $sp^3d^3$). Step 2 evaluates the interhalogen species. Halogens possess 7 valence electrons. In $\text{ClF}_3$, chlorine forms 3 single bonds, leaving $7 - 3 = 4$ non-bonding electrons, which gives $2$ lone pairs (T-shaped geometry, $sp^3d$). In $\text{BrF}_5$, bromine forms 5 single bonds, leaving $7 - 5 = 2$ electrons, which corresponds to $1$ lone pair (square pyramidal geometry, $sp^3d^2$). Step 3 sums the central lone pairs: $3 + 2 + 1 + 2 + 1 = 9$. Therefore, the total sum is 9.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Copper metal reacts distinctly with dilute $(\sim 20\%)$ and concentrated $(\sim 70\%)$ nitric acid according to: $3\text{Cu} + 8\text{HNO}_3(\text{dil}) \to 3\text{Cu}(\text{NO}_3)_2 + 2\text{NO} + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{Cu} + 4\text{HNO}_3(\text{conc}) \to \text{Cu}(\text{NO}_3)_2 + 2\text{NO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$. If $3.0\text{ mol}$ of copper is completely reacted with excess dilute $\text{HNO}_3$ in Reaction 1, and separately $3.0\text{ mol}$ of copper is completely reacted with excess concentrated $\text{HNO}_3$ in Reaction 2, what is the ratio of moles of nitric acid acting strictly as an oxidizing agent in Reaction 1 to that in Reaction 2?
questions.explanation: Step 1 distinguishes between nitric acid acting as a salt-forming acid versus an oxidizing agent. In Reaction 1 with dilute $\text{HNO}_3$: $3\text{ mol}$ of $\text{Cu}$ consumes $8\text{ mol}$ of $\text{HNO}_3$. Of these $8\text{ mol}$, $6\text{ mol}$ supply nitrate ions to form $3\text{Cu}(\text{NO}_3)_2$ without changing oxidation state (acting as acid), while $2\text{ mol}$ are reduced to $2\text{NO}$ ($N^{+5} \to N^{+2}$, gaining $3e^-$ each). Therefore, for $3.0\text{ mol}$ of $\text{Cu}$, the moles of $\text{HNO}_3$ acting as an oxidizing agent in Reaction 1 equal $2.0\text{ mol}$. Step 2 evaluates Reaction 2 with concentrated $\text{HNO}_3$: $1\text{ mol}$ of $\text{Cu}$ consumes $4\text{ mol}$ of $\text{HNO}_3$, wherein $2\text{ mol}$ form copper nitrate and $2\text{ mol}$ are reduced to $2\text{NO}_2$ ($N^{+5} \to N^{+4}$, gaining $1e^-$ each). Therefore, for $3.0\text{ mol}$ of $\text{Cu}$, the moles acting as an oxidizing agent equal $3.0 \times 2 = 6.0\text{ mol}$. Step 3 computes the ratio: $\frac{2.0}{6.0} = \frac{1}{3} = 1:3$. Hence, option C is correct. The distractor $2:3$ neglects to multiply the concentrated acid stoichiometry by the $3.0\text{ mol}$ of copper.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The bleaching action of sulfur dioxide on delicate fibers and flowers is temporary, whereas the bleaching action of chlorine water on colored textiles is permanent. Which statement correctly identifies the chemical mechanisms and the active reactive species generated in both cases?
options: A) $\text{SO}_2$ bleaches permanently by nascent oxygen, while $\text{Cl}_2$ bleaches temporarily by reduction with nascent hydrogen
B) $\text{SO}_2$ bleaches by physical adsorption of pigment molecules, while $\text{Cl}_2$ bleaches by precipitation of insoluble chloride salts
C) Both gases bleach by generating free chlorine radicals that cleave conjugated polyene double bonds indiscriminately
D) $\text{SO}_2$ bleaches temporarily by reduction via nascent hydrogen, while $\text{Cl}_2$ bleaches permanently by oxidation via nascent oxygen
questions.explanation: Step 1 investigates the mechanism of bleaching by sulfur dioxide. In the presence of moisture, sulfur dioxide reacts to produce nascent hydrogen: $\text{SO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \to \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 + 2[\text{H}]$. The nascent hydrogen reduces colored organic pigments to colorless leuco compounds: $\text{Color} + 2[\text{H}] \to \text{Colorless product}$. Upon exposure to aerial oxygen, the leuco compound is gradually re-oxidized back to the colored state, rendering the bleaching temporary. Step 2 investigates bleaching by chlorine water. Chlorine reacts with water to form hypochlorous acid: $\text{Cl}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \to \text{HCl} + \text{HOCl}$. Hypochlorous acid is unstable and decomposes to liberate nascent oxygen: $\text{HOCl} \to \text{HCl} + [\text{O}]$. The nascent oxygen permanently oxidizes colored matter into colorless oxidized degradation fragments: $\text{Color} + [\text{O}] \to \text{Colorless oxidized matter}$. Therefore, $\text{SO}_2$ bleaches by reduction (temporary) while $\text{Cl}_2$ bleaches by oxidation (permanent). Hence, statement D is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In the industrial Ostwald process for manufacturing nitric acid, ammonia is oxidized catalytically over a platinum-rhodium gauze at $1173\text{ K}$: $4\text{NH}_3(g) + 5\text{O}_2(g) \to 4\text{NO}(g) + 6\text{H}_2\text{O}(g)$. Nitric oxide is subsequently oxidized to $\text{NO}_2$ and absorbed in water: $3\text{NO}_2(g) + \text{H}_2\text{O}(l) \to 2\text{HNO}_3(aq) + \text{NO}(g)$, wherein the released $\text{NO}$ is recycled continuously back into the absorption loop with $100\%$ recovery efficiency. If the initial catalytic oxidation of ammonia proceeds with a $90.0\%$ conversion efficiency, what mass of $63.0\text{ wt}\%$ aqueous $\text{HNO}_3$ solution can be produced from $34.0\text{ kg}$ of pure ammonia feedstock?
questions.explanation: Step 1 calculates initial moles of ammonia: $n(\text{NH}_3) = \frac{34.0 \times 10^3\text{ g}}{17.0\text{ g/mol}} = 2000\text{ mol}$. At $90.0\%$ conversion in the primary oxidation reactor, moles of $\text{NO}$ entering the absorption circuit equal $0.900 \times 2000 = 1800\text{ mol}$. Step 2 tracks the absorption and recycle stoichiometry. The absorption reaction $3\text{NO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \to 2\text{HNO}_3 + \text{NO}$ converts $\frac{2}{3}$ of the nitrogen into nitric acid and leaves $\frac{1}{3}$ as $\text{NO}$. When recycled, the fraction converted over multiple passes follows an infinite geometric series: $\sum_{k=1}^\infty \frac{2}{3}\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{k-1} = \frac{2/3}{1 - 1/3} = 1.0$. Thus, with full recycle, the net overall reaction is $4\text{NO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{O}_2 \to 4\text{HNO}_3$, implying a $1:1$ molar conversion of entering $\text{NO}$ to $\text{HNO}_3$. Therefore, $n(\text{HNO}_3) = 1800\text{ mol}$. Step 3 computes the solution mass: pure $\text{HNO}_3$ mass $= 1800\text{ mol} \times 63.0\text{ g/mol} = 113.4\text{ kg}$. Since the solution contains $63.0\text{ wt}\%$ acid, dividing by $0.630$ gives total solution mass $= \frac{113.4\text{ kg}}{0.630} = 180.0\text{ kg}$. Hence, option A is correct. An answer of $200.0\text{ kg}$ assumes $100\%$ initial conversion, while $113.4\text{ kg}$ reports the mass of pure solute instead of the solution.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In the Contact process for the manufacture of sulfuric acid, sulfur trioxide produced via $2\text{SO}_2(g) + \text{O}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{SO}_3(g)$ is absorbed in concentrated $98.0\% \text{ H}_2\text{SO}_4$ to yield oleum ($\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_7$) rather than directly in water. What is the operational rationale for avoiding direct dissolution in water, and what mass of water must be added to $178.0\text{ kg}$ of pure oleum (molar mass $= 178.0\text{ g/mol}$) to produce an aqueous solution of $98.0\text{ wt}\%$ sulfuric acid?
options: A) Direct dissolution is endothermic and freezes the towers; requires $18.0\text{ kg}$ of water
B) Direct dissolution is violently exothermic and creates an unmanageable acid fog; requires $22.0\text{ kg}$ of water
C) Direct dissolution leads to reduction of $\text{SO}_3$ into toxic $\text{H}_2\text{S}$; requires $20.0\text{ kg}$ of water
D) Direct dissolution precipitates insoluble polymeric sulfur; requires $24.0\text{ kg}$ of water
questions.explanation: Step 1 identifies the physical-chemical reason: absorption of $\text{SO}_3$ directly in water is intensely exothermic ($\Delta H^\circ \approx -130\text{ kJ/mol}$). The massive heat release vaporizes the water, producing a persistent, highly corrosive mist of sulfuric acid droplets that is virtually impossible to condense or absorb efficiently. Step 2 evaluates the dilution stoichiometry: $\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_7 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \to 2\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$. Moles of oleum $= \frac{178.0 \times 10^3\text{ g}}{178.0\text{ g/mol}} = 1000\text{ mol}$. Reaction with $1000\text{ mol}$ ($18.0\text{ kg}$) of water yields $2000\text{ mol}$ of pure $100\% \text{ H}_2\text{SO}_4$, having a mass of $2000\text{ mol} \times 98.0\text{ g/mol} = 196.0\text{ kg}$. Step 3 calculates additional water needed to reach $98.0\text{ wt}\%$: total mass of $98.0\%$ solution $= \frac{196.0\text{ kg}}{0.980} = 200.0\text{ kg}$. Therefore, total water added to the initial $178.0\text{ kg}$ of oleum is $200.0 - 178.0 = 22.0\text{ kg}$. Hence, option B is correct. An answer of $18.0\text{ kg}$ produces $100\%$ acid rather than $98.0\%$ acid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the molecular structures of three oxoacids of phosphorus: pyrophosphoric acid ($\text{H}_4\text{P}_2\text{O}_7$), hypophosphoric acid ($\text{H}_4\text{P}_2\text{O}_6$), and pyrophosphorous acid ($\text{H}_4\text{P}_2\text{O}_5$). Let $a$ be the total number of bridging $\text{P-O-P}$ bonds, $b$ be the total number of direct $\text{P-P}$ bonds, and $c$ be the total number of direct $\text{P-H}$ bonds summed across all three molecules. Calculate the integer value of $(3a + 2b + c)$.
questions.explanation: Step 1 examines pyrophosphoric acid ($\text{H}_4\text{P}_2\text{O}_7$). Its structure is $(\text{HO})_2\text{P}(=\text{O})-\text{O}-\text{P}(=\text{O})(\text{OH})_2$. It contains $1$ bridging $\text{P-O-P}$ bond, $0$ direct $\text{P-P}$ bonds, and $0$ direct $\text{P-H}$ bonds. Step 2 examines hypophosphoric acid ($\text{H}_4\text{P}_2\text{O}_6$). Its structure is $(\text{HO})_2\text{P}(=\text{O})-\text{P}(=\text{O})(\text{OH})_2$. It contains $0$ bridging $\text{P-O-P}$ bonds, $1$ direct $\text{P-P}$ single bond, and $0$ direct $\text{P-H}$ bonds. Step 3 examines pyrophosphorous acid ($\text{H}_4\text{P}_2\text{O}_5$). Its structure is $\text{H}(\text{HO})\text{P}(=\text{O})-\text{O}-\text{P}(=\text{O})(\text{OH})\text{H}$. It contains $1$ bridging $\text{P-O-P}$ bond, $0$ direct $\text{P-P}$ bonds, and $2$ direct $\text{P-H}$ bonds. Summing across all three molecules yields $a = 1 + 0 + 1 = 2$, $b = 0 + 1 + 0 = 1$, and $c = 0 + 0 + 2 = 2$. Therefore, substituting these values into the expression yields $3(2) + 2(1) + 2 = 6 + 2 + 2 = 10$. Hence, the integer answer is 10.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the allotropic modifications and temperature-dependent behavior of elemental sulfur. Which statement provides an accurate structural and magnetic description of sulfur in its various phases?
options: A) Rhombic sulfur transforms irreversibly to monoclinic sulfur at $369\text{ K}$, and vapor $S_2$ molecules are diamagnetic due to completely paired bonding electrons
B) Engel's sulfur ($S_6$) possesses a planar hexagonal ring, while rhombic and monoclinic allotropes both contain open diradical octasulfur chains

C) Rhombic ($\alpha$) and monoclinic ($\beta$) sulfur exist in reversible equilibrium at the transition temperature $369\text{ K}$, both containing puckered crown $S_8$ rings, while elevated-temperature vapor $S_2$ is paramagnetic with two unpaired electrons in $\pi^*$ orbitals
D) Liquid sulfur displays a sharp decrease in viscosity at $433\text{ K}$ because crown $S_8$ rings disassemble entirely into isolated monatomic sulfur atoms
questions.explanation: Step 1 assesses the solid-state allotropes. Rhombic ($\alpha$) sulfur is stable below $369\text{ K}$, while monoclinic ($\beta$) sulfur is stable above $369\text{ K}$; at exactly $369\text{ K}$ (transition temperature), both forms can reversibly coexist. Both allotropes consist of puckered crown-shaped $S_8$ rings with an $\text{S-S-S}$ bond angle of $107^\circ$ and $\text{S-S}$ bond length of $204\text{ pm}$, differing primarily in the crystalline packing of the rings. Step 2 considers the $S_6$ modification. Engel's sulfur adopts a chair conformation rather than a planar hexagonal ring. Step 3 evaluates the vapor phase. At temperatures around $1000\text{ K}$, sulfur vapor contains predominantly diatomic $S_2$ molecules. According to molecular orbital theory, $S_2$ has an electronic configuration analogous to $O_2$ with two unpaired electrons residing in degenerate antibonding $\pi^*_{3px}$ and $\pi^*_{3py}$ orbitals, making it paramagnetic. Therefore, statement C is fully correct. Liquid sulfur at $433\text{ K}$ exhibits an increase in viscosity due to ring opening and polymerization into entangled chains.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: White phosphorus ($\text{P}_4$) is a translucent waxy solid that spontaneously ignites in air at $303\text{ K}$ and is stored under water, whereas polymeric red phosphorus is an odorless, non-poisonous solid stable in air up to $533\text{ K}$. Which statement correctly explains the underlying structural strain and thermodynamic factors governing this marked difference in reactivity?
options: A) White phosphorus contains $p\pi-p\pi$ multiple bonds between phosphorus atoms, whereas red phosphorus is stabilized by ionic lattice interactions
B) Red phosphorus has a larger heat of combustion than white phosphorus because of extensive hyperconjugation between phosphorus atoms
C) White phosphorus consists of planar square $\text{P}_4$ units with $90^\circ$ bond angles that induce torsional resonance stabilization

D) White phosphorus consists of discrete $\text{P}_4$ tetrahedra with bond angles compressed to $60^\circ$, creating severe angular strain of $\sim 49.5^\circ$ that lowers activation energy, whereas red phosphorus relieves strain via a polymeric network
questions.explanation: Step 1 examines the geometry of white phosphorus. The discrete $\text{P}_4$ molecule is a regular tetrahedron where each phosphorus atom is bonded to three other phosphorus atoms using nearly pure $3p$ orbitals. The internal $\text{P-P-P}$ bond angles are forced to be $60^\circ$, representing a severe deviation of $109.5^\circ - 60^\circ = 49.5^\circ$ from the ideal tetrahedral angle. This severe angular ring strain makes the $\text{P-P}$ bonds weak and energetically bent (banana bonds), conferring high enthalpy and lowering the activation barrier for combustion. Step 2 examines red phosphorus. When white phosphorus is heated to $\sim 573\text{ K}$ in an inert atmosphere, one $\text{P-P}$ bond per tetrahedron cleaves, linking the $\text{P}_4$ units into a polymeric chain of interconnected cages. This relieves the severe angular strain, rendering red phosphorus thermodynamically more stable, kinetically unreactive at room temperature, insoluble, and possessing a lower heat of combustion than white phosphorus. Therefore, statement D is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Stepwise partial and complete hydrolysis of xenon hexafluoride ($\text{XeF}_6$) produces three distinct xenon oxyfluorides and oxides: $\text{XeF}_6 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \to \text{P} + 2\text{HF}$; $\text{P} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \to \text{Q} + 2\text{HF}$; and $\text{Q} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \to \text{R} + 2\text{HF}$. What are the molecular formulas and VSEPR molecular shapes of species $\text{P}$, $\text{Q}$, and $\text{R}$, respectively?
options: A) $\text{P} = \text{XeOF}_4$ (square pyramidal), $\text{Q} = \text{XeO}_2\text{F}_2$ (see-saw), and $\text{R} = \text{XeO}_3$ (trigonal pyramidal)
B) $\text{P} = \text{XeOF}_4$ (tetrahedral), $\text{Q} = \text{XeO}_2\text{F}_2$ (square planar), and $\text{R} = \text{XeO}_3$ (planar)
C) $\text{P} = \text{XeO}_2\text{F}_2$ (square planar), $\text{Q} = \text{XeOF}_4$ (T-shaped), and $\text{R} = \text{XeO}_3$ (trigonal planar)
D) $\text{P} = \text{XeOF}_4$ (octahedral), $\text{Q} = \text{XeO}_2\text{F}_2$ (bent), and $\text{R} = \text{XeO}_4$ (tetrahedral)
questions.explanation: Step 1 identifies the stepwise hydrolysis products. In each step, an oxygen atom replaces two fluorine atoms: $\text{P} = \text{XeOF}_4$, $\text{Q} = \text{XeO}_2\text{F}_2$, and $\text{R} = \text{XeO}_3$. Step 2 applies VSEPR theory to $\text{XeOF}_4$. Xenon has 8 valence electrons, forming 1 double bond to oxygen (2 electrons), 4 single bonds to fluorine (4 electrons), and retaining $1$ lone pair. Steric number $= 5 + 1 = 6$ ($sp^3d^2$ hybridization). The octahedral electron arrangement with one lone pair gives a square pyramidal shape. Step 3 applies VSEPR to $\text{XeO}_2\text{F}_2$. Xenon forms 2 double bonds to oxygen (4 electrons), 2 single bonds to fluorine (2 electrons), and retains $1$ lone pair. Steric number $= 4 + 1 = 5$ ($sp^3d$). Trigonal bipyramidal electron geometry with the lone pair and oxygens equatorial produces a see-saw molecular shape. Step 4 applies VSEPR to $\text{XeO}_3$. Xenon forms 3 double bonds to oxygen (6 electrons) and retains $1$ lone pair. Steric number $= 3 + 1 = 4$ ($sp^3$), yielding a trigonal pyramidal shape. Therefore, option A is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: When solid xenon tetrafluoride reacts with liquid water, it disproportionates according to: $6\text{XeF}_4(s) + 12\text{H}_2\text{O}(l) \to 2\text{XeO}_3(s) + 4\text{Xe}(g) + 3\text{O}_2(g) + 24\text{HF}(aq)$. When $6.0\text{ mol}$ of $\text{XeF}_4$ undergoes complete reaction with water, what is the total number of moles of gaseous products $(\text{Xe} + \text{O}_2)$ evolved?
questions.explanation: Step 1 examines the balanced chemical equation. The reaction states: $6\text{XeF}_4 + 12\text{H}_2\text{O} \to 2\text{XeO}_3 + 4\text{Xe} + 3\text{O}_2 + 24\text{HF}$. In this equation, $6\text{ mol}$ of $\text{XeF}_4$ produces $4\text{ mol}$ of xenon gas and $3\text{ mol}$ of oxygen gas, while $\text{XeO}_3$ is a solid and $\text{HF}$ remains in the aqueous solution. Step 2 sums the gaseous products evolved per $6.0\text{ mol}$ of $\text{XeF}_4$: moles of $\text{Xe}(g) = 4.0\text{ mol}$, and moles of $\text{O}_2(g) = 3.0\text{ mol}$. Therefore, the total moles of gaseous products equal $n_{\text{gas}} = n(\text{Xe}) + n(\text{O}_2) = 4.0 + 3.0 = 7\text{ mol}$. Hence, the resulting integer value is 7.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the oxoacids of chlorine: hypochlorous acid ($\text{HClO}$), chlorous acid ($\text{HClO}_2$), chloric acid ($\text{HClO}_3$), and perchloric acid ($\text{HClO}_4$). Which statement correctly describes the variation in their acidic strengths and their thermodynamic oxidizing abilities as the oxidation state of chlorine increases from $+1$ to $+7$?
options: A) Both acidic strength and oxidizing ability increase continuously from $\text{HClO}$ to $\text{HClO}_4$

B) Acidic strength increases in the order $\text{HClO} < \text{HClO}_2 < \text{HClO}_3 < \text{HClO}_4$, whereas oxidizing ability decreases in the order $\text{HClO} > \text{HClO}_2 > \text{HClO}_3 > \text{HClO}_4$
C) Acidic strength decreases because conjugate bases become less stable, while oxidizing ability increases due to higher chlorine electronegativity
D) Acidic strength remains constant because all four species contain exactly one ionizable hydroxyl proton, while oxidizing ability peaks at $\text{HClO}_2$
questions.explanation: Step 1 evaluates acidic strength. The conjugate bases are $\text{ClO}^-$, $\text{ClO}_2^-$, $\text{ClO}_3^-$, and $\text{ClO}_4^-$. As the number of terminal oxo oxygen atoms increases from 0 in $\text{ClO}^-$ to 3 in $\text{ClO}_4^-$, the negative charge becomes progressively delocalized over 4 equivalent oxygen atoms through resonance ($d\pi-p\pi$ overlap). Increased conjugate base stability directly enhances proton dissociation, yielding the acidity order $\text{HClO} < \text{HClO}_2 < \text{HClO}_3 < \text{HClO}_4$ ($pK_a$ drops from $\sim 7.5$ for $\text{HClO}$ to $\sim -10$ for $\text{HClO}_4$). Step 2 evaluates oxidizing power. Reduction involves breaking $\text{Cl-O}$ bonds and altering coordinate geometry. The perchlorate ion ($\text{ClO}_4^-$) is highly symmetrical, resonance-stabilized, and sterically compact, creating high kinetic and thermodynamic activation barriers for reduction in dilute solution. Conversely, $\text{HClO}$ possesses a weak, polarized single $\text{Cl-O}$ bond that readily releases oxygen, rendering hypochlorous acid the strongest and fastest oxidizing agent. Therefore, oxidizing power decreases as oxidation number increases: $\text{HClO} > \text{HClO}_2 > \text{HClO}_3 > \text{HClO}_4$. Hence, option B is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Chlorine trifluoride ($\text{ClF}_3$) is an aggressive fluorinating reagent used industrially to convert uranium metal into uranium hexafluoride ($\text{UF}_6$) for nuclear fuel enrichment: $\text{U}(s) + 3\text{ClF}_3(l) \to \text{UF}_6(g) + 3\text{ClF}(g)$. Which statement correctly accounts for the molecular geometry of $\text{ClF}_3$ and the stoichiometric volume of gaseous products liberated at STP when $0.50\text{ mol}$ of uranium reacts completely?
options: A) $\text{ClF}_3$ is trigonal planar; reaction produces $11.2\text{ L}$ of $\text{UF}_6$ and $11.2\text{ L}$ of $\text{ClF}$
B) $\text{ClF}_3$ is trigonal pyramidal; reaction produces $22.4\text{ L}$ of $\text{UF}_6$ and $33.6\text{ L}$ of $\text{ClF}$
C) $\text{ClF}_3$ is T-shaped with two equatorial lone pairs; reaction produces $11.2\text{ L}$ of $\text{UF}_6$ and $33.6\text{ L}$ of $\text{ClF}$
D) $\text{ClF}_3$ is see-saw shaped; reaction produces $22.4\text{ L}$ of dry gaseous mixture
questions.explanation: Step 1 applies VSEPR theory to $\text{ClF}_3$. The central chlorine atom has 7 valence electrons, forming 3 single covalent bonds with fluorine atoms and retaining $(7 - 3)/2 = 2$ non-bonding lone pairs. The steric number is $3 + 2 = 5$, corresponding to a trigonal bipyramidal electron-pair geometry with $sp^3d$ hybridization. To minimize severe $90^\circ$ lone pair–lone pair and lone pair–bonding pair repulsions, both lone pairs occupy equatorial positions, bending the axial $\text{F-Cl-F}$ angle to approximately $175^\circ$ and resulting in a T-shaped molecular geometry. Step 2 evaluates the reaction stoichiometry: $1\text{ mol}$ of $\text{U}$ produces $1\text{ mol}$ of $\text{UF}_6(g)$ and $3\text{ mol}$ of $\text{ClF}(g)$. For $0.50\text{ mol}$ of $\text{U}$: $n(\text{UF}_6) = 0.50\text{ mol}$, and $n(\text{ClF}) = 3 \times 0.50 = 1.50\text{ mol}$. Step 3 computes STP volumes: $V(\text{UF}_6) = 0.50\text{ mol} \times 22.4\text{ L/mol} = 11.2\text{ L}$, and $V(\text{ClF}) = 1.50\text{ mol} \times 22.4\text{ L/mol} = 33.6\text{ L}$. Therefore, option C is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: When chlorine gas is bubbled into a hot concentrated aqueous solution of sodium hydroxide, it undergoes disproportionation according to: $3\text{Cl}_2 + 6\text{NaOH} \to 5\text{NaCl} + \text{NaClO}_3 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$. If $18.0\text{ moles}$ of $\text{Cl}_2$ reacts completely, calculate the positive difference between the moles of chlorine atoms reduced to chloride and the moles of chlorine atoms oxidized to chlorate.
questions.explanation: Step 1 tracks the oxidation state transitions. In elemental $\text{Cl}_2$, the oxidation state of chlorine is $0$. In sodium chloride ($\text{NaCl}$), chlorine is in the $-1$ state (reduction: $0 \to -1$). In sodium chlorate ($\text{NaClO}_3$), chlorine is in the $+5$ state (oxidation: $0 \to +5$). Step 2 evaluates the stoichiometry per reaction formula: $3\text{ moles}$ of $\text{Cl}_2$ contains $6\text{ moles}$ of chlorine atoms. Of these 6 atoms, 5 atoms are reduced to $\text{Cl}^-$ and 1 atom is oxidized to $\text{ClO}_3^-$. Step 3 calculates quantities for $18.0\text{ moles}$ of $\text{Cl}_2$: total moles of chlorine atoms equal $18.0 \times 2 = 36.0\text{ mol}$. Moles of chlorine atoms reduced $= \frac{5}{6} \times 36.0 = 30.0\text{ mol}$. Moles of chlorine atoms oxidized $= \frac{1}{6} \times 36.0 = 6.0\text{ mol}$. Therefore, the difference between reduced and oxidized chlorine atoms is $30.0 - 6.0 = 24.0\text{ mol}$. Hence, the required integer value is 24.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Zinc metal reacts differently with dilute $(\sim 20\%)$ and concentrated $(\sim 70\%)$ nitric acid: $4\text{Zn} + 10\text{HNO}_3(\text{dil}) \to 4\text{Zn}(\text{NO}_3)_2 + \text{N}_2\text{O} + 5\text{H}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{Zn} + 4\text{HNO}_3(\text{conc}) \to \text{Zn}(\text{NO}_3)_2 + 2\text{NO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$. If $4.0\text{ mol}$ of zinc metal is reacted with excess dilute $\text{HNO}_3$ in Vessel A, and separately $4.0\text{ mol}$ of zinc metal is reacted with excess concentrated $\text{HNO}_3$ in Vessel B, what are the volumes of dry gaseous products collected at STP from Vessel A and Vessel B, respectively?
options: A) $89.6\text{ L}$ from Vessel A and $89.6\text{ L}$ from Vessel B
B) $44.8\text{ L}$ from Vessel A and $179.2\text{ L}$ from Vessel B
C) $22.4\text{ L}$ from Vessel A and $89.6\text{ L}$ from Vessel B
D) $22.4\text{ L}$ from Vessel A and $179.2\text{ L}$ from Vessel B
questions.explanation: Step 1 calculates gas evolution in Vessel A (dilute $\text{HNO}_3$). Stoichiometry shows $4\text{ mol}$ of $\text{Zn}$ yields $1\text{ mol}$ of nitrous oxide gas ($\text{N}_2\text{O}$). For $4.0\text{ mol}$ of $\text{Zn}$, exactly $1.0\text{ mol}$ of $\text{N}_2\text{O}$ is formed. Volume at STP $= 1.0\text{ mol} \times 22.4\text{ L/mol} = 22.4\text{ L}$. Step 2 calculates gas evolution in Vessel B (concentrated $\text{HNO}_3$). Stoichiometry shows $1\text{ mol}$ of $\text{Zn}$ produces $2\text{ mol}$ of nitrogen dioxide gas ($\text{NO}_2$). For $4.0\text{ mol}$ of $\text{Zn}$, moles of $\text{NO}_2$ formed equal $4.0 \times 2 = 8.0\text{ mol}$. Volume at STP $= 8.0\text{ mol} \times 22.4\text{ L/mol} = 179.2\text{ L}$. Therefore, Vessel A yields $22.4\text{ L}$ while Vessel B yields $179.2\text{ L}$. Hence, option D is correct. An answer of $89.6\text{ L}$ for Vessel B mistakenly assumes $1\text{ mol}$ of $\text{NO}_2$ per mole of $\text{Zn}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: An air sample containing toxic carbon monoxide is analyzed quantitatively by passing it through a tube packed with solid diiodine pentoxide ($\text{I}_2\text{O}_5$) at $423\text{ K}$: $\text{I}_2\text{O}_5(s) + 5\text{CO}(g) \to \text{I}_2(s) + 5\text{CO}_2(g)$. The liberated iodine is absorbed in aqueous $\text{KI}$ and titrated against $0.020\text{ M}$ sodium thiosulfate solution: $\text{I}_2 + 2\text{Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3 \to 2\text{NaI} + \text{Na}_2\text{S}_4\text{O}_6$. If titration requires exactly $25.0\text{ mL}$ of the thiosulfate solution to reach the starch end point, what mass of carbon monoxide (molar mass $= 28.0\text{ g/mol}$) was present in the analyzed sample?
options: A) $35.0\text{ mg}$
B) $7.0\text{ mg}$
C) $70.0\text{ mg}$
D) $14.0\text{ mg}$
questions.explanation: Step 1 calculates moles of sodium thiosulfate consumed: $n(\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-}) = 0.0250\text{ L} \times 0.020\text{ mol/L} = 5.0 \times 10^{-4}\text{ mol}$. Step 2 links thiosulfate to liberated iodine. Stoichiometrically, $1\text{ mol}$ of $\text{I}_2$ reacts with $2\text{ mol}$ of $\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-}$, yielding $n(\text{I}_2) = \frac{5.0 \times 10^{-4}}{2} = 2.5 \times 10^{-4}\text{ mol}$. Step 3 relates iodine to carbon monoxide: $1\text{ mol}$ of $\text{I}_2$ is liberated by $5\text{ mol}$ of $\text{CO}$. Therefore, $n(\text{CO}) = 5 \times n(\text{I}_2) = 5 \times (2.5 \times 10^{-4}) = 1.25 \times 10^{-3}\text{ mol}$. Step 4 converts moles to mass: substituting the molar mass of $\text{CO}$ yields $\text{mass} = 1.25 \times 10^{-3}\text{ mol} \times 28.0\text{ g/mol} = 0.0350\text{ g} = 35.0\text{ mg}$. Hence, option A is correct. A mass of $7.0\text{ mg}$ forgets the stoichiometric factor of 5 for $\text{CO}$, while $70.0\text{ mg}$ forgets the factor of $\frac{1}{2}$ for thiosulfate.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Phosphorus pentachloride ($\text{PCl}_5$) reacts characteristically with hydroxyl-containing organic compounds: $\text{ROH} + \text{PCl}_5 \to \text{RCl} + \text{POCl}_3 + \text{HCl}$, and with carboxylic acids: $\text{RCOOH} + \text{PCl}_5 \to \text{RCOCl} + \text{POCl}_3 + \text{HCl}$. If $1.0\text{ mol}$ of ethanol ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$) and $1.0\text{ mol}$ of acetic acid ($\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$) are treated in separate reaction flasks with stoichiometric quantities of $\text{PCl}_5$, what are the total moles of phosphoryl chloride ($\text{POCl}_3$) and gaseous $\text{HCl}$ produced across both reactions combined?
options: A) $1.0\text{ mol }\text{POCl}_3$ and $1.0\text{ mol }\text{HCl}$
B) $2.0\text{ mol }\text{POCl}_3$ and $2.0\text{ mol }\text{HCl}$
C) $2.0\text{ mol }\text{POCl}_3$ and $4.0\text{ mol }\text{HCl}$
D) $1.0\text{ mol }\text{POCl}_3$ and $2.0\text{ mol }\text{HCl}$
questions.explanation: Step 1 examines the reaction with ethanol: $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH} + \text{PCl}_5 \to \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Cl} + \text{POCl}_3 + \text{HCl}$. Reacting $1.0\text{ mol}$ of ethanol consumes $1.0\text{ mol}$ of $\text{PCl}_5$, producing $1.0\text{ mol}$ of ethyl chloride, $1.0\text{ mol}$ of $\text{POCl}_3$, and $1.0\text{ mol}$ of $\text{HCl}$. Step 2 examines the reaction with acetic acid: $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH} + \text{PCl}_5 \to \text{CH}_3\text{COCl} + \text{POCl}_3 + \text{HCl}$. Reacting $1.0\text{ mol}$ of acetic acid consumes $1.0\text{ mol}$ of $\text{PCl}_5$, producing $1.0\text{ mol}$ of acetyl chloride, $1.0\text{ mol}$ of $\text{POCl}_3$, and $1.0\text{ mol}$ of $\text{HCl}$. Step 3 sums the inorganic products across both flasks: total $n(\text{POCl}_3) = 1.0 + 1.0 = 2.0\text{ mol}$, and total $n(\text{HCl}) = 1.0 + 1.0 = 2.0\text{ mol}$. Therefore, $2.0\text{ mol}$ of $\text{POCl}_3$ and $2.0\text{ mol}$ of $\text{HCl}$ are formed. Hence, option B is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In the chemistry of polythionic acids, consider one molecule of dithionic acid ($\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_6$) and one molecule of trithionic acid ($\text{H}_2\text{S}_3\text{O}_6$). Let $N_{\text{S-S}}$ be the total count of direct sulfur–sulfur single bonds present combined in both molecules, and let $N_{\text{S=O}}$ be the total count of sulfur–oxygen double bonds combined in both molecules. Calculate the integer value of $(2 N_{\text{S-S}} + N_{\text{S=O}})$.
questions.explanation: Step 1 examines dithionic acid ($\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_6$). Its structural formula is $\text{HO}-\text{SO}_2-\text{SO}_2-\text{OH}$. The two sulfur atoms are joined by a single direct $\text{S-S}$ covalent bond, giving $1$ $\text{S-S}$ bond. Each $-\text{SO}_2-$ group carries two $\text{S=O}$ double bonds and one $\text{S-OH}$ bond, yielding $2 \times 2 = 4$ $\text{S=O}$ double bonds. Step 2 examines trithionic acid ($\text{H}_2\text{S}_3\text{O}_6$). Its structural formula is $\text{HO}-\text{SO}_2-\text{S}-\text{SO}_2-\text{OH}$. The central divalent sulfur atom is bonded to two terminal sulfonyl groups via two $\text{S-S}$ single bonds, giving $2$ $\text{S-S}$ bonds. The two terminal sulfonyl groups contain $2 \times 2 = 4$ $\text{S=O}$ double bonds, while the central sulfur atom carries no oxygen atoms. Step 3 sums the bond counts: $N_{\text{S-S}} = 1 + 2 = 3$, and $N_{\text{S=O}} = 4 + 4 = 8$. Therefore, substituting these counts into the expression yields $2(3) + 8 = 6 + 8 = 14$. Hence, the integer answer is 14.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The industrial synthesis of ammonia via the Haber-Bosch process is governed by the equilibrium: $\text{N}_2(g) + 3\text{H}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3(g) \quad (\Delta H^\circ = -92.4\text{ kJ/mol})$. Operating conditions are maintained at approximately $700\text{ K}$ and $200\text{ atm}$ in the presence of an iron oxide catalyst promoted with $\text{K}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$. What is the primary thermodynamic reason for avoiding operation at room temperature ($300\text{ K}$), and how do $K_p$ and the equilibrium mole fraction of $\text{NH}_3$ change if pressure is increased to $300\text{ atm}$ at $700\text{ K}$?
options: A) At $300\text{ K}$, $\Delta G^\circ$ becomes positive preventing reaction; increasing pressure increases $K_p$
B) At $300\text{ K}$, ammonia decomposes explosively; increasing pressure decreases the mole fraction of $\text{NH}_3$

C) Although lower temperature thermodynamically favors $\text{NH}_3$ formation, the reaction rate at $300\text{ K}$ is impractically slow due to the inert $\text{N}\equiv\text{N}$ triple bond; increasing pressure leaves $K_p$ unchanged while increasing the equilibrium mole fraction of $\text{NH}_3$
D) High temperature is required because the reaction is endothermic; increasing pressure leaves both $K_p$ and mole fraction unchanged
questions.explanation: Step 1 evaluates temperature kinetics versus thermodynamics. Because the forward reaction is exothermic ($\Delta H^\circ < 0$), lowering temperature increases the equilibrium constant $K_p$, favoring ammonia formation thermodynamically. However, dinitrogen possesses an exceptionally strong $\text{N}\equiv\text{N}$ triple bond with a bond dissociation enthalpy of $941.4\text{ kJ/mol}$, resulting in a prohibitively high activation energy barrier. At $300\text{ K}$, the uncatalyzed or even catalyzed rate is practically zero. Thus, $700\text{ K}$ serves as the optimum compromise between reaction velocity and thermodynamic yield. Step 2 evaluates pressure effects. The equilibrium constant $K_p$ is a thermodynamic function strictly of temperature; therefore, increasing pressure from $200\text{ atm}$ to $300\text{ atm}$ at constant temperature leaves $K_p$ unchanged. In contrast, the forward reaction proceeds with a reduction in gaseous moles ($4\text{ mol} \to 2\text{ mol}$). According to Le Chatelier's principle, higher pressure shifts the equilibrium forward, thereby increasing the equilibrium mole fraction of $\text{NH}_3$. Hence, option C is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Dinitrogen pentoxide ($\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$) displays striking structural polymorphism depending on its physical state. Which statement accurately identifies its constitution, hybridizations, and geometries in the crystalline solid state versus the isolated gaseous phase?
options: A) Solid $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$ is covalent with cyclic peroxide rings, while gaseous $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$ consists of dissociated $\text{NO}_2$ and $\text{NO}_3$ free radicals
B) Solid $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$ is an ionic solid $[\text{NO}]^+[\text{NO}_4]^-$, while gaseous $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$ is a linear molecule with $sp$ hybridization
C) Solid $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$ is a coordination polymer with octahedral nitrogen, while gaseous $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$ is an ionic gas pair

D) Solid $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$ is an ionic crystal formulated as nitronium nitrate $[\text{NO}_2]^+[\text{NO}_3]^-$, while gaseous $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$ consists of covalent molecules with two planar $-\text{NO}_2$ units linked by a bent $\text{N-O-N}$ bridge
questions.explanation: Step 1 examines crystalline solid $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$. X-ray diffraction confirms that solid $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$ is entirely ionic, consisting of nitronium cations $[\text{NO}_2]^+$ and nitrate anions $[\text{NO}_3]^-$. In $[\text{NO}_2]^+$, the nitrogen atom has steric number 2 ($sp$ hybridized) and adopts a strictly linear geometry with an $\text{O-N-O}$ angle of $180^\circ$. In $[\text{NO}_3]^-$, nitrogen has steric number 3 ($sp^2$ hybridized) and adopts a trigonal planar geometry with $120^\circ$ bond angles. Step 2 examines gaseous $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$. In the gas phase, it exists as discrete covalent molecules featuring two planar $-\text{NO}_2$ groups linked through a central bridging oxygen atom ($\text{O}_2\text{N}-\text{O}-\text{NO}_2$). The bridging $\text{N-O-N}$ bond angle is bent at approximately $112^\circ$, and the terminal nitrogen atoms are $sp^2$ hybridized. Therefore, solid $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$ is nitronium nitrate while gaseous $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$ is a bent bridged covalent molecule. Hence, option D is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: When solid bismuth trichloride ($\text{BiCl}_3$) is dissolved in an excess of pure water, a dense white turbidity of bismuth oxychloride precipitates according to the reversible equilibrium: $\text{BiCl}_3(aq) + \text{H}_2\text{O}(l) \rightleftharpoons \text{BiOCl}(s) + 2\text{HCl}(aq)$. How can this turbid suspension be converted back into a clear transparent solution, and what fundamental periodic trend does this hydrolysis behavior illustrate across the Group 15 trichlorides?
options: A) By adding concentrated hydrochloric acid ($\text{HCl}$); it illustrates that metallic and basic character increase down Group 15 from non-metallic $\text{NCl}_3$ to metallic $\text{BiCl}_3$
B) By adding sodium hydroxide ($\text{NaOH}$); it illustrates that acidity increases down Group 15
C) By boiling vigorously to expel $\text{Cl}_2$ gas; it illustrates the inert pair effect of phosphorus
D) By bubbling $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ gas to dissolve $\text{BiOCl}$; it illustrates that bismuth forms stable polysulfides
questions.explanation: Step 1 applies Le Chatelier's principle to the hydrolysis equilibrium. The reversible reaction generates hydrochloric acid: $\text{BiCl}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightleftharpoons \text{BiOCl}\downarrow + 2\text{HCl}$. Adding concentrated $\text{HCl}$ introduces a high concentration of common $\text{H}^+$ and $\text{Cl}^-$ ions, which drives the equilibrium backward toward reactants, completely dissolving the white precipitate of $\text{BiOCl}$ and yielding a clear solution of $\text{BiCl}_3$ (or $[\text{BiCl}_4]^-$ complex). Step 2 contrasts Group 15 trichloride hydrolysis: $\text{NCl}_3$ undergoes irreversible hydrolysis with water to produce $\text{NH}_3$ and $\text{HOCl}$ because chlorine is more electropositive than nitrogen. $\text{PCl}_3$ hydrolyzes irreversibly to give $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_3$ and $\text{HCl}$. In contrast, $\text{BiCl}_3$ undergoes partial, reversible hydrolysis to an insoluble basic bismuthyl salt ($\text{BiOCl}$), demonstrating that bismuth has predominant metallic character and basic oxide/hydroxide tendencies. Therefore, option A is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Three distinct ammonium salts undergo thermal decomposition upon controlled heating: Reaction 1: $(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7 \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{N}_2 + \text{Cr}_2\text{O}_3 + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}$; Reaction 2: $\text{NH}_4\text{NO}_2 \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{N}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$; and Reaction 3: $\text{NH}_4\text{NO}_3 \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{N}_2\text{O} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Which statement correctly analyzes the oxidation state transitions occurring in nitrogen across these three reactions?
options: A) In all three reactions, nitrogen undergoes disproportionation from an intermediate state to $-3$ and $+5$

B) Reaction 1 is an intramolecular redox reaction where $\text{N}$ is oxidized from $-3$ to $0$; Reactions 2 and 3 are internal comproportionations where nitrogen in $-3$ and $+3$ yields $\text{N}_2$ ($0$), and nitrogen in $-3$ and $+5$ yields $\text{N}_2\text{O}$ ($+1$), respectively
C) Nitrogen is reduced in Reaction 1 from $+3$ to $0$, whereas chromium is oxidized from $+3$ to $+6$
D) Reactions 1, 2, and 3 are non-redox ligand substitution processes that liberate trapped atmospheric nitrogen
questions.explanation: Step 1 examines Reaction 1: in $(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$, nitrogen is in the $-3$ oxidation state (in $\text{NH}_4^+$) and chromium is in the $+6$ oxidation state (in $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$). Upon heating, nitrogen is oxidized from $-3$ to $0$ in $\text{N}_2$ (loss of $3e^-$ per N), while chromium is reduced from $+6$ to $+3$ in $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_3$ (gain of $3e^-$ per Cr). This constitutes an intramolecular redox reaction. Step 2 examines Reaction 2: in $\text{NH}_4\text{NO}_2$, the cation contains nitrogen in the $-3$ state and the anion contains nitrogen in the $+3$ state. They comproportionate to produce $\text{N}_2$ where both nitrogen atoms end in the $0$ oxidation state. Step 3 examines Reaction 3: in $\text{NH}_4\text{NO}_3$, nitrogen in $\text{NH}_4^+$ ($-3$) and nitrogen in $\text{NO}_3^-$ ($+5$) comproportionate to yield nitrous oxide ($\text{N}_2\text{O}$), where nitrogen has an oxidation state of $+1$. Therefore, statement B provides the exact oxidation transitions. Hence, option B is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Elemental iodine is sparingly soluble in pure water but dissolves readily in aqueous potassium iodide solution due to the formation of the triiodide polyhalide ion: $\text{KI}(aq) + \text{I}_2(s) \rightleftharpoons \text{KI}_3(aq)$. What is the geometry, hybridization of the central iodine atom in $\text{I}_3^-$, and the relative thermodynamic stability trend of the trihalide anions $\text{Cl}_3^-$, $\text{Br}_3^-$, and $\text{I}_3^-$?
options: A) Trigonal planar geometry, $sp^2$ hybridization; stability follows $\text{Cl}_3^- > \text{Br}_3^- > \text{I}_3^-$
B) Bent geometry with $104.5^\circ$ angle, $sp^3$ hybridization; stability follows $\text{Br}_3^- > \text{I}_3^- > \text{Cl}_3^-$
C) Linear geometry, $sp^3d$ hybridization with three equatorial lone pairs; stability follows $\text{I}_3^- > \text{Br}_3^- > \text{Cl}_3^-$
D) T-shaped geometry, $sp^3d$ hybridization; stability follows $\text{Cl}_3^- \approx \text{Br}_3^- \approx \text{I}_3^-$
questions.explanation: Step 1 applies VSEPR theory to $\text{I}_3^-$. The central iodine atom possesses 7 valence electrons plus 1 electron from the negative formal charge, totaling 8 valence electrons. It forms 2 single covalent bonds with the terminal iodine atoms, leaving $(8 - 2)/2 = 3$ non-bonding lone pairs. The steric number is $2 + 3 = 5$, indicating $sp^3d$ hybridization and trigonal bipyramidal electron-pair geometry. Step 2 determines the molecular shape: to minimize electron repulsion, the 3 bulky lone pairs occupy the equatorial plane at $120^\circ$ angles to each other. The two terminal iodine atoms occupy the axial positions, yielding a strictly linear molecular geometry with an $\text{I-I-I}$ bond angle of $180^\circ$. Step 3 evaluates the stability sequence. Polyhalide formation involves electron donation into low-lying empty d-orbitals and polarizability of the halogen atoms. Large, highly polarizable atoms disperse negative charge much more effectively. Consequently, stability follows the sequence $\text{I}_3^- > \text{Br}_3^- > \text{Cl}_3^-$ (in fact, $\text{Cl}_3^-$ is extremely unstable and dissociates readily). Hence, option C is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Sulfur tetrafluoride hydrolyzes readily with water to produce sulfur dioxide and hydrofluoric acid: $\text{SF}_4 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \to \text{SO}_2 + 4\text{HF}$. In contrast, sulfur hexafluoride ($\text{SF}_6$) is kinetically inert to water even at elevated temperatures. If $2.5\text{ mol}$ of pure $\text{SF}_4$ is completely hydrolyzed in water, and the resulting acidic solution is titrated to complete neutralization with standard aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ (forming $\text{Na}_2\text{SO}_3$ and $\text{NaF}$), calculate the total moles of $\text{NaOH}$ consumed.
questions.explanation: Step 1 determines the moles of acidic products produced from $2.5\text{ mol}$ of $\text{SF}_4$. From the hydrolysis stoichiometry: $1\text{ mol}$ of $\text{SF}_4$ produces $1\text{ mol}$ of $\text{SO}_2$ and $4\text{ mol}$ of $\text{HF}$. Therefore, $2.5\text{ mol}$ of $\text{SF}_4$ yields $n(\text{SO}_2) = 2.5\text{ mol}$ and $n(\text{HF}) = 2.5 \times 4 = 10.0\text{ mol}$. Step 2 establishes the neutralization stoichiometry with sodium hydroxide: $\text{SO}_2$ is a diprotic acidic oxide neutralizing according to $\text{SO}_2 + 2\text{NaOH} \to \text{Na}_2\text{SO}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$, consuming $2\text{ mol}$ of $\text{NaOH}$ per mole of $\text{SO}_2$. Hydrofluoric acid is a monoprotic acid neutralizing according to $\text{HF} + \text{NaOH} \to \text{NaF} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$, consuming $1\text{ mol}$ of $\text{NaOH}$ per mole of $\text{HF}$. Step 3 calculates the total moles of $\text{NaOH}$ required: $n(\text{NaOH}) = 2 \times n(\text{SO}_2) + 1 \times n(\text{HF}) = 2(2.5) + 1(10.0) = 5.0 + 10.0 = 15.0\text{ mol}$. Therefore, exactly 15 moles of $\text{NaOH}$ are consumed. Hence, the integer answer is 15.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the disproportionation equilibria and redox thermodynamic tendencies of halogen oxoacids and oxoanions in aqueous solutions. Which of the following statements is/are correct?
options: A) In cold dilute aqueous alkali, chlorine disproportionates into chloride and hypochlorite ($Cl_2 + 2OH^- \to Cl^- + ClO^- + H_2O$), whereas in hot concentrated alkali, hypochlorite rapidly disproportionates further to chloride and chlorate ($3ClO^- \to 2Cl^- + ClO_3^-$)

B) The rate of disproportionation of hypohalite ions to halate and halide increases dramatically down Group 17: $ClO^- < BrO^- < IO^-$, such that hypoiodite ($IO^-$) disproportionates almost instantaneously even at $273\text{ K}$

C) In acidic aqueous solution, hypochlorous acid ($\text{HClO}$) undergoes thermodynamic disproportionation according to $3\text{HClO} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{HCl} + \text{HClO}_3$, driven by the high thermodynamic stability of chloric acid
D) Aqueous perchloric acid ($\text{HClO}_4$) readily disproportionates at room temperature into dichlorine heptoxide ($\text{Cl}_2\text{O}_7$) and chloric acid
questions.explanation: Step 1 evaluates temperature dependence of chlorine disproportionation in base. In cold dilute $\text{NaOH}$ ($sim 288\text{ K}$), chlorine disproportionates to chloride and hypochlorite: $\text{Cl}_2 + 2\text{OH}^- \to \text{Cl}^- + \text{ClO}^- + \text{H}_2\text{O}$. Upon heating to $\sim 343\text{ K}$, hypochlorite disproportionates into chloride and chlorate: $3\text{ClO}^- \to 2\text{Cl}^- + \text{ClO}_3^-$, giving the net hot reaction $3\text{Cl}_2 + 6\text{OH}^- \to 5\text{Cl}^- + \text{ClO}_3^- + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Therefore, statement A is correct. Step 2 evaluates the group trend in hypohalite disproportionation. As halogen size increases down Group 17, the activation energy for disproportionation decreases sharply. While $\text{ClO}^-$ requires heating, $\text{BrO}^-$ disproportionates moderately at room temperature, and $\text{IO}^-$ disproportionates almost instantaneously even at $0^\circ\text{C}$ to $\text{I}^-$ and $\text{IO}_3^-$. Hence, statement B is correct. Step 3 examines acidic hypochlorous acid. Applying Latimer diagram standard reduction potentials, $E^\circ(\text{HClO}/\text{Cl}_2) = +1.63\text{ V}$ and $E^\circ(\text{HClO}_3/\text{HClO}) = +1.21\text{ V}$. Because the potential on the right is higher than that on the left, $\text{HClO}$ is thermodynamically unstable toward disproportionation into $\text{HCl}$ and $\text{HClO}_3$: $3\text{HClO} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{HCl} + \text{HClO}_3$ with $\Delta G^\circ < 0$. Therefore, statement C is correct. Step 4 examines perchloric acid. In $\text{HClO}_4$, chlorine resides in its highest possible group oxidation state ($+7$). It cannot be oxidized further; hence disproportionation is chemically impossible. Therefore, statement D is incorrect. Solving together confirms A, B, and C are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Neil Bartlett's landmark preparation of the first true noble gas compound was based on a thermodynamic and structural analogy between molecular oxygen and xenon. Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding this breakthrough and noble gas reactivity?
options: A) Bartlett discovered that deep-red platinum hexafluoride ($\text{PtF}_6$) vapor spontaneously oxidized molecular oxygen to yield the ionic compound dioxygenyl hexafluoroplatinate, $\text{O}_2^+[\text{PtF}_6]^-$

B) The first ionization enthalpy of molecular oxygen ($1175\text{ kJ/mol}$) is remarkably comparable to the first ionization enthalpy of xenon ($1170\text{ kJ/mol}$), providing the thermodynamic rationale that $\text{PtF}_6$ could oxidize xenon

C) The molecular diameter of the $\text{O}_2$ molecule ($sim 4.0\text{ \AA}$) is nearly identical to the van der Waals diameter of the xenon atom, allowing similar lattice enthalpy stabilization in the solid state
D) Helium and neon form analogous crystalline hexafluoroplatinate salts under standard laboratory conditions because their ionization enthalpies are comparable to that of xenon
questions.explanation: Step 1 reviews the historical discovery: in 1962, Neil Bartlett observed that the powerful oxidizing agent platinum hexafluoride ($\text{PtF}_6$) oxidized $\text{O}_2$ to synthesize the ionic solid dioxygenyl hexafluoroplatinate: $\text{O}_2 + \text{PtF}_6 \to \text{O}_2^+[\text{PtF}_6]^-$. Therefore, statement A is correct. Step 2 analyzes the ionization enthalpy parameters. The first ionization enthalpy of molecular oxygen ($\text{O}_2 \to \text{O}_2^+ + e^-$) is $1175\text{ kJ/mol}$, while the first ionization enthalpy of xenon ($\text{Xe} \to \text{Xe}^+ + e^-$) is $1170\text{ kJ/mol}$. Because the ionization enthalpy of xenon is marginally lower than that of oxygen, Bartlett reasoned that $\text{PtF}_6$ should oxidize xenon with comparable or greater thermodynamic feasibility. Hence, statement B is correct. Step 3 examines lattice energy considerations. The effective van der Waals radius of xenon ($2.16\text{ \AA}$) yields a diameter closely matching that of the dioxygen molecule ($sim 4.0\text{ \AA}$). This size congruence ensures that the lattice enthalpy of the resulting solid salt $[\text{Xe}]^+[\text{PtF}_6]^-$ compensates for the endothermic ionization enthalpy. Thus, statement C is correct. Step 4 examines helium and neon. The first ionization enthalpies of helium ($2372\text{ kJ/mol}$) and neon ($2080\text{ kJ/mol}$) are far too enormous to be compensated by any chemical lattice enthalpy, rendering analogous salt formation impossible. Therefore, statement D is incorrect. Solving together confirms A, B, and C are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Xenon fluorides exhibit versatile coordination chemistry by functioning both as fluoride ion donors toward strong Lewis acids and as fluoride ion acceptors toward strong Lewis bases. Which of the following statements is/are correct?
options: A) Reaction of $\text{XeF}_6$ with strong Lewis acid fluoride acceptors like $\text{SbF}_5$ and $\text{AsF}_5$ produces $[\text{XeF}_5]^+[\text{SbF}_6]^-$ and $[\text{XeF}_5]^+[\text{AsF}_6]^-$, where the cation $[\text{XeF}_5]^+$ has a square pyramidal geometry

B) Reaction of $\text{XeF}_6$ with alkali metal fluorides $\text{MF}$ (where $\text{M} = \text{Na}, \text{K}, \text{Rb}, \text{Cs}$) produces heptafluoroxenate(VI) salts $\text{M}^+[\text{XeF}_7]^-$, where $\text{XeF}_6$ acts as a Lewis acid
C) Xenon difluoride ($\text{XeF}_2$) acts as a fluoride donor toward phosphorus pentafluoride to form $[\text{XeF}]^+[\text{PF}_6]^-$, where the cation $[\text{XeF}]^+$ is linear
D) In the cation $[\text{XeF}_5]^+$, the xenon atom possesses two non-bonding lone pairs and adopts a pentagonal planar molecular geometry
questions.explanation: Step 1 evaluates fluoride donor behavior of $\text{XeF}_6$: $\text{XeF}_6 + \text{SbF}_5 \to [\text{XeF}_5]^+[\text{SbF}_6]^-$. In the cation $[\text{XeF}_5]^+$, xenon has 8 valence electrons minus 1 electron from formal positive charge $= 7$ electrons. It forms 5 single bonds with fluorine, leaving $(7 - 5)/2 = 1$ non-bonding lone pair. Steric number $= 5 + 1 = 6$ ($sp^3d^2$ hybridization). Octahedral electron-pair geometry with 1 lone pair yields a square pyramidal shape. Therefore, statement A is correct. Step 2 evaluates fluoride acceptor behavior of $\text{XeF}_6$: $\text{XeF}_6 + \text{CsF} \to \text{Cs}^+[\text{XeF}_7]^-$. Here, $\text{XeF}_6$ accepts a fluoride ion from the ionic fluoride donor $\text{CsF}$, demonstrating Lewis acidity. In $[\text{XeF}_7]^-$, xenon has $8 + 1 = 9$ electrons, forming 7 bonds with 1 lone pair (capped octahedral / distorted pentagonal bipyramidal geometry). Thus, statement B is correct. Step 3 examines $\text{XeF}_2$ donor behavior: $\text{XeF}_2 + \text{PF}_5 \to [\text{XeF}]^+[\text{PF}_6]^-$. In $[\text{XeF}]^+$, xenon forms a single bond to fluorine; diatomic ions are strictly linear. Hence, statement C is correct. Step 4 assesses statement D. As derived in Step 1, $[\text{XeF}_5]^+$ possesses exactly $1$ lone pair and is square pyramidal, not pentagonal planar (which would require 2 lone pairs). Therefore, statement D is incorrect. Solving together confirms A, B, and C are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the molecular architectures, protic basicities, and redox properties of the oxoacids of phosphorus. Which of the following statements is/are correct?
options: A) Hypophosphorous acid ($\text{H}_3\text{PO}_2$) contains one $\text{P-OH}$ bond and two direct $\text{P-H}$ bonds; it acts as a monoprotic acid and a potent reducing agent capable of precipitating silver from $\text{AgNO}_3$

B) Orthophosphorous acid ($\text{H}_3\text{PO}_3$) contains two $\text{P-OH}$ bonds and one direct $\text{P-H}$ bond; upon thermal heating, it undergoes disproportionation into orthophosphoric acid ($\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$) and phosphine ($\text{PH}_3$)

C) Pyrophosphoric acid ($\text{H}_4\text{P}_2\text{O}_7$) is a tetrabasic acid possessing four $\text{P-OH}$ bonds, two $\text{P=O}$ bonds, and one bridging $\text{P-O-P}$ bond, exhibiting zero reducing properties
D) Cyclotrimetaphosphoric acid ($(\text{HPO}_3)_3$) possesses a planar ring composed of alternating phosphorus atoms with three direct $\text{P-P}$ bonds
questions.explanation: Step 1 analyzes hypophosphorous acid ($\text{H}_3\text{PO}_2$). Its Lewis structure is $\text{H}_2\text{P}(=\text{O})(\text{OH})$. It features $1$ $\text{P-OH}$ bond (monobasic, donating $1\text{ H}^+$ in water), $1$ $\text{P=O}$ double bond, and $2$ direct $\text{P-H}$ bonds. The presence of two $\text{P-H}$ bonds gives it strong reducing capacity, reducing $\text{Ag}^+$ to metallic $\text{Ag}$: $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_2 + 4\text{Ag}^+ + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \to \text{H}_3\text{PO}_4 + 4\text{Ag}\downarrow + 4\text{H}^+$. Thus, statement A is correct. Step 2 analyzes orthophosphorous acid ($\text{H}_3\text{PO}_3$). Its structure is $\text{HP}(=\text{O})(\text{OH})_2$, possessing $2$ ionizable $\text{P-OH}$ bonds (dibasic) and $1$ $\text{P-H}$ bond. When heated, it disproportionates: $4\text{H}_3\text{PO}_3 \xrightarrow{\Delta} 3\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4 + \text{PH}_3$ ($P^{+3} \to P^{+5} + P^{-3}$). Thus, statement B is correct. Step 3 analyzes pyrophosphoric acid ($\text{H}_4\text{P}_2\text{O}_7$). Its structure is $(\text{HO})_2\text{P}(=\text{O})-\text{O}-\text{P}(=\text{O})(\text{OH})_2$. It contains $4$ ionizable $\text{P-OH}$ bonds (tetrabasic), $2$ terminal $\text{P=O}$ bonds, $1$ bridging $\text{P-O-P}$ linkage, and no $\text{P-H}$ bonds, meaning it has zero reducing character. Thus, statement C is correct. Step 4 analyzes cyclotrimetaphosphoric acid ($(\text{HPO}_3)_3$). Its cyclic framework consists of alternating phosphorus and oxygen atoms ($-\text{P}-\text{O}-\text{P}-\text{O}-\text{P}-\text{O}-$), containing three bridging $\text{P-O-P}$ bonds and zero $\text{P-P}$ bonds. Therefore, statement D is incorrect. Hence, A, B, and C are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
